page.layout: One page of text, single column; running head above the text; catchword at the foot right ("raq̃" appears as a line-end fragment, not a catchword). No margin notes.

main_text.p: cere nō potest. Nec minus hoc nomi ne tamen ualuit ille in explodendis opinionū periculis, imo multo fœli-cius, simul & ijs satisfaciens qui con-tendebant, & reliquos confirmans si qui fluctuabant. Quantulū iam Hel-uidius, Iouinianus, Pelagius, feredis suis opinionibus, proficere ualue-runt, emergentibus semel ac lectis Hieronymi, tanto cum nitore elima-tis uoluminibus: Quæ tam late graf-fata hærefis, non ilico, ceu adempta uoce, obticuit, semel in theatrum pro-deunte Augustino, uel fulminante in Ecclesijs Hieronymo, in libris nō minus fere formidabili, quàm qui-uis est in foro iudex? Sed nunc litera-rias has uelitationes amisimus, imo ut uerius dicam, amisimus in Eccle-sia proceres, Augustino, ac Hiero-nymo similes, qui stylo, ac eloquētia uelitari sciant, in quorum subijt ui-cem posteritas talis, quæ defendit plerunq̃, quę iudicare nequeat, me-raq̃

page.notes: The first line is a running head; the scan is a fragment at the top ("cere nō potest" continues from the previous page). Several words are uncertain in the scan (e.g. "feredis", "subijt", "Eccle-sia"), and the scan's ink is faint in places. The final word "raq̃" appears set apart at the lower right and is treated as a catchword.
